recentItems.title: Man City found guilty of financial rule breaches
recentItems.description:
Manchester City have been found guilty of all charges relating to serious breaches of the English Premier League's financial rules over a period of nine seasons.

In addition, the league revealed that the club has also been found guilty on three of four charges concerning their failure to co-operate with the investigation.

Let's look at this and other stories making headlines in the world of sport.

recentItems.title: Two key Bafana players unavailable
recentItems.description:
A second successive victory in their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign will put Bafana Bafana in the pound seats.

South Africa face minnows Eritrea in a Group D encounter in Cairo, Egypt, this evening.

The lowly-ranked East Africans have never qualified for an AFCON tournament, and Bafana should fancy their chances.

But Pitso Mosimane will be without the services of the injured Teboho Mokoena and Aubrey Modiba.

recentItems.title: Massive fuel price hikes expected next month
recentItems.description:
South African motorists are facing another major blow at the pumps, with petrol prices potentially rising by around R3 a litre next week. 95 petrol could reach the R30 mark as higher oil prices and a weaker rand push fuel costs sharply high. 

To unpack the bigger impact, let's bring in Johann Els, Group Chief Economist at PSG Financial Services.

recentItems.title: Lesotho helping small businesses tap into Africa's growing market
recentItems.description:
Lesotho is sharpening its focus on small businesses as it looks to unlock opportunities under regional trade agreements and the African Continental Free Trade Area. 

The Trade and Industry Ministry is hosting a three-day workshop aimed at helping small businesses compete, expand and tap into Africa's growing market. 

SABC News correspondent Rapelang Radebe reports from Maseru.

recentItems.title: CRL Rights Commission welcomes Ramaphosa’s four-point plan to tackle GBVF
recentItems.description:
The CRL Rights Commission has welcomed President Cyril Ramaphosa's four-point plan to tackle South Africa's high rate of gender-based violence and femicide.

Commission chairperson Thoko Mkhwanazi‑Xaluva says the plan must be closely monitored to ensure that the commitments are met. 

She explains that the existing legislation has failed to protect both the victims and survivors of the GBVF scourge.

recentItems.title: Tshuma case postponed to October 21 for finalisation of plea agreement
recentItems.description:
The Johannesburg Magistrate's Court has postponed the case against alleged UK fugitive Ndodana Mkhanyisi Tshuma to October 21 for the finalisation of his plea agreement.

Tshuma had pleaded guilty to Firearms Control Act-related charges, including possessing an unlicensed pistol and ammunition when he was arrested in Johannesburg in June.

The Zimbabwean-British national is wanted by UK authorities for the murders of his wife, Zandile, and their two daughters, 15-year-old Natalie and five-year-old Nala in Bedford, England, in July. 

He had abandoned his bail application and remains in custody.

recentItems.title: Madlanga Commission | Sibanyoni questioned over alleged PUTCO stake demand and extortion
recentItems.description:
The cross examination of Joe "Ferrari" Sibanyoni by the Madlanga Commission is on its second day and proceedings have continued on the theme of alleged organised crime networks and extortion by the Mpumalanga taxi boss.

The Inquiry flighted a viral video where Sibanyoni is heard demanding a 30 percent stake in PUTCO bus services during a meeting with President Cyril Ramaphosa and Minister Gwede Mantashe.

recentItems.title: Restaurant Incident | Parly committee demands action from SANRAL
recentItems.description:
The South African National Roads Agency Limited (SANRAL) was grilled by Parliament's Transport Portfolio Committee, about a recent incident, in which one of its contractors was caught on camera, making death threats against women in a Joburg restaurant. 

MPs want to know how far SANRAL's management is in dealing with the matter. 

Earlier this month, the chairperson of Moriel Infrastructure Group, which has two contracts with SANRAL, was filmed harassing, intimidating and threatening a group of women. 

SANRAL top management and its Board appeared before the committee today, to discuss procurement and consequence management.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Tanzania institutes compulsory travel insurance
recentItems.description:
Foreign visitors to mainland Tanzania will need compulsory travel insurance from October 1st, under new regulations issued by the Ministry of Finance. 

The move follows a similar scheme in the semi-autonomous Islands of Zanzibar, and comes weeks after Kenya adopted its own insurance requirement for foreign visitors.
